sources.offline: pyproject.toml, tools/site/package.json, tools/site/package-lock.json, software/vendor/manifest.json, kit hash records, software/vendor/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md, software/vendor/upstreams/registry.yaml, docs/research/landscape.json, published Markdown

limits: A clean report is not proof of safety: advisory databases (OSV, the npm registry) only know what has been reported.
Licences come from licence files and registry metadata (GitHub, PyPI, npm), matched by keyword; they are not a legal review.
Link checks see status codes and redirects, not content: a parked or replaced page that answers 200 passes. Domain expiry is not checked.
GitHub links are checked at repository level; a missing file or anchor inside a live repository is not seen.
Python versions are checked at the newest release and the lowest release our range allows, not at every version in between.

Transitive Python dependencies are checked at the versions deps.dev resolves for our newest direct releases; an existing environment may hold other versions, and --installed checks only the installed versions of our direct dependencies.

Libraries bundled inside a vendored file (DOMPurify and KaTeX inside mermaid.min.js) are checked at the versions its receipt records; whether the bundling library reaches the affected code is not assessed.
Repository settings (secret scanning, Dependabot) are read only with an admin token; the weekly workflow cannot see them.
Offline mode checks only what the checkout shows (pins, hashes, licence files, lockfile, link schemes, install advice).

findings.subject: npm:esbuild
findings.title: esbuild runs an install script
findings.action: Read the script; in CI prefer npm ci --ignore-scripts where the package works without it.
findings.accepted: Maintainer-only tools/mermaid compiler 0.28.2, not a production-site dependency. Its complete install.js was read on 2026-11-07 (#322), SHA256 612294e278914443bdcf81cb17f54afec34dbdd2ebd999a6ee187912320cc315: it validates or downloads/installs a platform executable and can rewrite its wrapper. The dedicated context and provenance CI use npm ci --ignore-scripts, so this hook is not executed. The producer resolves the installed exact optional platform binary and verifies its SHA256 against the pinned esbuild package's binaryHashes before execution; missing/mismatched input fails instead of invoking the hook. This fingerprint includes tools/mermaid/package.json and covers only 0.28.2's known hook, not an advisory, registry drift, a future hook or another context that runs install scripts. (2026-11-07)

findings.subject: npm:fsevents
findings.title: fsevents runs an install script (only on darwin)
findings.action: Read the script; in CI prefer npm ci --ignore-scripts where the package works without it.
findings.accepted: Optional, macOS-only dependency of Playwright (os: darwin), so CI and Linux machines never install it. Read on 2026-11-01 (#151): the registry's manifest for 2.3.2 lists install "node-gyp rebuild" (gypfile), but the tarball the lockfile pins (its sha512 matches) has no binding.gyp and its package.json has no install script; it ships a prebuilt fsevents.node, so npm runs nothing at install. The fingerprint is 2.3.2's: when Playwright moves to another fsevents, the finding comes back to be read again. (2026-11-01)

findings.subject: repo:dependabot-npm
findings.title: Dependabot does not watch npm (tools/site/package.json)
findings.action: Add a weekly npm entry targeting dev (owner decision: it opens PRs).
findings.accepted: Deliberate maintenance-pass policy under issues 153 and 322, reaffirmed 2026-11-07: retain grouped weekly GitHub Actions version PRs, without starting recurring npm version-PR campaigns during backlog closure. The weekly supply-chain workflow audits both explicit npm locks online and keeps one findings issue; pin updates still require independent review, provenance and browser CI. This accepts only the absence of the npm version-update configuration, not an advisory, stale pin or failed audit. It does not claim Dependabot monitors these manifests or that dependency-graph/SBOM discovery is verified; issue 153 retains that unresolved evidence. Security-fix PRs are enabled separately but their coverage is not proven here. (2026-11-07)

findings.subject: npm:khroma
findings.title: khroma declares no licence
findings.action: Read the exact locked archive licence before relying on it; bind an exception to this context and archive.
findings.accepted: Metadata omission in the exact tools/mermaid lock entry khroma 2.1.0. The npm archive pinned by sha512-Ls993zuzfayK269Svk9hzpeGUKob/sIgZzyHYdjQoAdQetRKpOLj+k/QQQ/6Qi0Yz65mlROrfd+Ev+1+7dz9Kw== contains its complete MIT licence, copyright Fabio Spampinato and Andrew Maney. Read on 2026-11-07: node_modules/khroma/license SHA256 66b333b0f66759a0b710459e03f7029abe17f4358114a128d2c972e642961b49. The unchanged renderer BUILD.json records that exact licence and THIRD-PARTY-LICENSES.txt retains the text. This fingerprint binds the owning manifest, version, resolved archive and integrity; another context, version or archive needs a new reading. It accepts only absent registry/lock licence metadata, not package integrity failures, advisories or a general legal review. (2026-11-07)
